title: Functions, scope, and closures — map
intro: This module covers how JavaScript defines functions, binds parameters, resolves names through lexical scope, and keeps outer variables alive via closures. The loop-with-var trap and scope-chain-vs-call-stack distinction are top interview topics. Higher-order functions and IIFEs build on closures; recursion stresses the call stack limit.

conceptCards.title: Function forms
conceptCards.summary: Declaration (hoisted), expression (value), arrow (lexical this). Pick by hoisting and this needs.

conceptCards.title: Parameters and rest
conceptCards.summary: Defaults apply for undefined only. Rest collects extras into a real Array.

conceptCards.title: Lexical scope chain
conceptCards.summary: Names resolve through outer environments at write time. Scope chain ≠ call stack.

conceptCards.title: Closures and loop trap
conceptCards.summary: Functions remember outer bindings. var in loops shares one i; let fixes per iteration.
conceptCards.example: for (let i=0; i<3; i++) setTimeout(() => i)

conceptCards.title: IIFE and module pattern
conceptCards.summary: Immediately invoked wrapper for private scope. Return public API from closure.
conceptCards.example: const api = (function () { let s; return { get: () => s }; })();

conceptCards.title: Higher-order functions
conceptCards.summary: Functions that take or return functions. once, debounce, map built on closures.

conceptCards.title: Recursion and stack
conceptCards.summary: Each call pushes a frame. No reliable TCO in V8. Use loops for deep depth.
conceptCards.example: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
